newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy lower house passes Banco di Napoli decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy lower house passes Banco di Napoli decree.

text.p: Italy's lower house of parliament approved a decree law on Thursday on a rescue plan for the ailing southern bank, Bank di Napoli, and officials said it would now pass to the upper Senate for final approval.

Thursday's vote followed a confidence vote in the chamber on Wednesday that the government called and won to sweep aside 1,001 blocking amendments which had been submitted by the separatist Northern League party.
Thursday's vote in the Chamber of Deputies, where Prime Minister Romano Prodi depends on the hard left Communist Refoundation party for support, was 303 to 203 with 17 abstentions, officials said.
Prodi's centre-left government has a majority in its own right in the Senate.
The Treasury wants to inject two trillion lire ($1.3 billion) of state funds into Banco di Napoli and privatise the heavily indebted bank before the end of the year.
The decree had been set to expire on November 24. It cannot be resurrected after that as a result of a recent Constitutional Court ruling, which prevents decrees from being resubmitted.
